mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month indicates strong labor market conditions, which historically correlates with positive economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where the labor market shows strong growth.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals increased consumer spending, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month suggests increased economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points in a month, coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000, signals a tightening labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where both trigger conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a broad-based increase in demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where both trigger conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month, coupled with a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2%, signals inflationary pressure and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both trigger conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met.
